featured_reviews.name: Nithin M Agarwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
My Google Review # 000323.

Visited this “HIDDEN EDUCATION HEAVEN” few weeks ago to get details for enrolling my kid. And I must admit, that their “gurukul” model, their spacious classrooms and the lush greenery spread in some 14 acres, took me back to my childhood days.

Do you miss having an Olympic-sized swimming pool, a dedicated games building and a separate music arena for your child? Well, MIT-VIS Mira Road is exactly how a school needs to be designed. Only when you visit personally, you understand what is missing in most of the Mumbai’s “Boutique Schools” now-a-days.

The concrete road leading to the premises is 90% complete. The entire campus is properly guarded with electric fences and tall two-layered boundary walls. The administration staff was prompt in giving us a quick tour of the school and the admission counsellor also patiently cleared all our “schooling” doubts.

After briefing ourselves with Mr Karad’s vision, his achievements and after interacting with the energetic teaching staff, aptly guided by the Principal, we were assured that MIT-VIS is here not only to stay, but soon become a beacon of knowledge to most of the Mumbai’s young students and other institutions.

Will surely recommend MIT-VIS, if you cherish a holistic learning for your kid and not just academia-based teaching.

Date of Experience # 22 Feb 2024.

Recently, students with pending fees were denied access to their exam papers in class, while the rest of their classmates reviewed theirs. This act, done in front of the entire class, was deeply embarrassing and emotionally hurtful for the children involved.

While we completely understand the school’s policy regarding fees and open house access, humiliating a child publicly can never be justified. Policies should never come at the cost of a student’s dignity or mental well-being.

As parents, we are aware of our dues and are doing our best — especially in times where education costs rise nearly 12% each year, making it a challenge for many families. All we expect from a reputed institution like Ostwal Academy is empathy and fair treatment toward every student, irrespective of financial status.

This isn’t just about fees — it’s about the values being taught within the walls of a school.
I truly hope the management takes this feedback seriously and ensures that no child ever has to go through such humiliation again. Children deserve respect, compassion, and understanding — not public embarrassment.

This is not written in anger, but in genuine disappointment and hope for change.
